answer: In an agent economy, each participant must emit a verifiable activity pulse every epoch by performing costly on-chain computations or stake-locking, which generates an echo of their prior validated actions in the reputation graph. This creates a rising economic tide that floods low-stake Sybil clusters with prohibitive bonding costs, as attackers cannot cheaply replicate the cumulative stake and historical echo trail required to influence consensus without burning real resources proportional to their fake identities.
